text: You're alive because a rock landed in exactly the wrong spot.
66 million years ago, an asteroid about 10 kilometres wide hit what is now Mexico.
say: Sixty-six million years ago, an asteroid about ten kilometres wide hit what is now Mexico.
asr: Sixty-six million years ago, an asteroid about ten kilometres wide hit what is now Mexico.

text: But here's the problem. On a classroom globe, that rock would be a grain of sand. How does a grain of sand kill the dinosaurs?
The answer was under the sea. The seabed was packed with sulfur and oil-rich rock, and the impact threw it into the sky.
Soot and sulfur blocked the Sun for months. One study found only about 13 percent of Earth's surface would have been that deadly.
say: Soot and sulfur blocked the Sun for months. One study found only about thirteen percent of Earth's surface would have been that deadly.
asr: Soot and sulfur blocked the Sun for months. One study found only about thirteen percent of Earth's surface would have been that deadly.

text: It didn't just hit Earth. It hit one of the worst places it could.
Now imagine you're alive in that darkness. No sunlight. Plants are dying. What do you eat?
Big animals starved first. Almost nothing on land bigger than a large dog made it.
The survivors were small. They hid in burrows and lived on seeds, insects and rotting plants.
And one of those small survivors was our ancestor.
So what if the asteroid had missed?
Mammals had already lived beside dinosaurs for over 100 million years, and most never got bigger than a badger. Every big job on land was taken.
say: Mammals had already lived beside dinosaurs for over a hundred million years, and most never got bigger than a badger. Every big job on land was taken.
asr: Mammals had already lived beside dinosaurs for over a hundred million years, and most never got bigger than a badger. Every big job on land was taken.

text: When the dinosaurs vanished, those jobs opened up. Within a million years, mammals were growing much bigger.
No asteroid, and that door may never open. No apes. No cities. No you.
One last thing. Everyone says the dinosaurs died out. But did they?
A few small feathered ones made it through the dark.
So look outside. That pigeon on your window is a dinosaur. And it survived the same rock that made you possible.
